selected_edition.article_title: High-resolution (1 km) Köppen-Geiger maps for 1901–2099 based on constrained CMIP6 projections
selected_edition.edition_note: Figshare v2 says the data were updated in January 2026 to correct a small calculation error; it refers to an associated article correction for details. The exact correction details were not independently recovered in this bounded review.
selected_edition.product: Historical and future Köppen–Geiger class-map GeoTIFF archive; the article also describes associated confidence products
selected_edition.scope: Global land raster extent; no Australia-specific mask, denominator, or coverage percentage in the examined metadata.

existing_pinned_evidence.coverage_statement: Four global historical Köppen–Geiger normals: 1901–1930, 1931–1960, 1961–1990, 1991–2020; latest may be labeled a separate modern reference.
existing_pinned_evidence.comparison: Downloaded and hashed the exact public version 2 archive. Its SHA-256 equals the existing pinned archive hash above; no replacement or re-preparation was made.

sources.name: Figshare current version 2 GeoTIFF archive
sources.retention: Downloaded for full-object hash and read-only archive listing/header inspection. Temporary copy is outside the repository; restore exact bytes from URL and compare size and SHA-256. No source raster or archive is included in Git.

observations: 1. Existing source inventory and source receipt reviewed; exact current Figshare v2 archive hash equals the previously pinned source archive hash.
2. Article publication date is 2023-10-23; Figshare version 2 is a later data edition published/modified 2026-01-14 and notes a small calculation correction.

3. Historical map directories are 1901–1930, 1931–1960, 1961–1990 and 1991–2020; outputs are climatological categories, not annual weather observations. Article-documented confidence outputs are not inspected in the selected GeoTIFF ZIP.
4. Paper method derives each normal from adjusted temperature and precipitation reference climatologies and a modal combination; source-input observation coverage does not enlarge output intervals.
5. Each historical 0.00833333-degree TIFF is a 43200x21600 EPSG:4326 global grid; Australia lies within the described global land raster footprint. No Australia-only mask/area denominator was found.
6. Archive future directories begin 2041–2070 and 2071–2099 under SSPs; no 2021–2040 or 2025 classification output exists.
7. The 1991–2020 normal remains a normal ending in 2020; it is not a 2025 observation. No extrapolation or interpolation is supported.
8. Both article and data record identify CC BY 4.0; public archive download needs no private access.

9. Station-validation aggregates and WorldAtlas global location counts are not Australia-specific accuracy or territory denominators. Per-cell input provenance and Australian support percentages were not in examined metadata.
header_method: Read-only GDAL gdalinfo -json -noct on the four selected global historical GeoTIFF entries through /vsizip/; inspected ZIP central-directory filenames and timestamps. No cropping, class sampling, transformation, preparation, or import was performed.
uncertainties: No Australian territorial boundary or area denominator was independently evaluated; the global raster extent only establishes source footprint coverage, not a country-level coverage percentage.
The v2 record identifies a small calculation correction but the associated correction details were not recovered in this bounded review.
Global station-validation rates do not quantify Australia-only map error; no Australia-specific accuracy guarantee is claimed.
ZIP internal file timestamps are package/file metadata and are not climate observation dates.
